Simulate two-dimensional natural convection in a unit square cavity using OpenFOAM with the buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam solver.
The case targets the de Vahl Davis benchmark at Rayleigh number Ra = 1e5.
The fluid is air-like with Pr = 0.71, beta = 3.39e-3 1/K (based on T_ref = 295 K), and kinematic viscosity nu = 4.8e-4 m2/s chosen so that Ra = g·beta·ΔT·L³·Pr/nu² equals 1e5 with L = 1 m, ΔT = 10 K, and g = 9.81 m/s2.
Gravity acts downwards as g = (0 -9.81 0) m/s2.
Use the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy with reference temperature T_ref = 295 K.
The left wall is hot with fixedValue temperature T = 300 K, the right wall is cold with fixedValue temperature T = 290 K.
The top and bottom walls are adiabatic with zeroGradient temperature boundary conditions.
All four walls use noSlip velocity boundary conditions.
The mesh is a uniform structured 100 x 100 grid with simpleGrading 1 1 1.
The mesh is 2D with 1 cell in the z-direction and empty boundary conditions on the front and back patches.
Run in laminar mode (RAS model laminar) with no turbulence model.
Initialize the flow at rest with uniform velocity (0 0 0) and uniform temperature T = 295 K.
Run the transient solver until steady state is reached by monitoring the Nusselt number at the cold wall and stopping when its relative change falls below 0.1% over a monitoring window.
Set a generous endTime as a safety cap (several hundred convective time units) so the job terminates even if steady state detection fails.
Verify from monitored quantities (Nusselt number, mid-plane velocity extrema) that the final solution is steady before comparing against the de Vahl Davis benchmark data.
